76394-the-love-of-an-uncrowned-queen.title: first published from the originals_)
76394-the-love-of-an-uncrowned-queen.creator: Unknown
76394-the-love-of-an-uncrowned-queen.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. But it was not until six years ago, in 1897, that I lighted by chance (while turning over old volumes in a second-hand bookshop at Leipzig) upon the fact that an unpublished correspondence between Sophie Dorothea and Königsmarck existed.

arxiv-2007-09568.title: Only Time Will Tell: Credible Dynamic Signaling This paper is based on chapter 3 of the author’s Ph.D. thesis. The author thanks Nemanja Antić, Eddie Dekel, Jeffrey Ely, Yingni Guo, Nicolas Inostroza, Johan Lagerlöf, Alexey Makarin, Wojciech Olszewski, Marco Schwarz, Ludvig Sinander, Peter Norman Sø
arxiv-2007-09568.creator: Egor Starkov
arxiv-2007-09568.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Egor Starkov. This paper characterizes informational outcomes in a model of dynamic signaling with vanishing commitment power. It shows that contrary to popular belief, informative equilibria with payoff-relevant signaling can exist without requiring unreasonable off-path beliefs. The paper provides a sharp characterization of possible separating equilibria: all signaling must take place through attrition, when the weakest type mixes between revealing own type and pooling with the stronger types.

arxiv-2107-08724.title: Estimation of high-dimensional change-points under a group sparsity structure
arxiv-2107-08724.creator: Hanqing Cai, Tengyao Wang
arxiv-2107-08724.description: Abstract Change-points are a routine feature of ‘big data’ observed in the form of high-dimensional data streams. In many such data streams, the component series possess group structures and it is natural to assume that changes only occur in a small number of all groups.

arxiv-2111-04044.title: Parallelize Single-Site Dynamics up to Dobrushin Criterion
arxiv-2111-04044.creator: Hongyang Liu, Yitong Yin
arxiv-2111-04044.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hongyang Liu, Yitong Yin. Single-site dynamics are canonical Markov chain based algorithms for sampling from high-dimensional distributions, such as the Gibbs distributions of graphical models. We introduce a simple and generic parallel algorithm that faithfully simulates single-site dynamics.

arxiv-2203-10410.title: Language-Preserving Reduction Rules for Block-Structured Workflow Nets
arxiv-2203-10410.creator: Sander J.J. Leemans
arxiv-2203-10410.description: Abstract Process models are used by human analysts to model and analyse behaviour, and by machines to verify properties such as soundness, liveness or other reachability properties, and to compare their expressed behaviour with recorded behaviour within business processes of organisations.

arxiv-2203-17064.title: Atmosphere Loss in Oblique Super-Earth Collisions 2021 Atmosphere Loss in Oblique Super-Earth Collisions – F
arxiv-2203-17064.creator: Thomas R. Denman, Zoë M. Leinhardt, Philip J. Carter
arxiv-2203-17064.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thomas R. Denman, Zoë M. Leinhardt, Philip J. Carter. Using smoothed particle hydrodynamics we model giant impacts of Super-Earth mass rocky planets between an atmosphere-less projectile and an atmosphere-rich target. In this work we present results from head-on to grazing collisions. The results of the simulations fall into two broad categories: 1) one main post-collision remnant containing material from target and projectile; 2) two main post-collision remnants resulting from ‘erosive hit-and-run’ collisions.

arxiv-2305-15296.title: MultiFusion: Fusing Pre-Trained Models for Multi-Lingual, Multi-Modal Image Generation
arxiv-2305-15296.creator: Marco Bellagente, Manuel Brack, Hannah Teufel, Felix Friedrich, Björn Deiseroth, Constantin Eichenberg, Andrew Dai, Robert J.N. Baldock, Souradeep Nanda, Koen Oostermeijer, Andres Felipe Cruz-Salinas, Patrick Schramowski, Kristian Kersting, Samuel Weinbach
arxiv-2305-15296.description: Abstract The recent popularity of text-to-image diffusion models (DM) can largely be attributed to the intuitive interface they provide to users. The intended generation can be expressed in natural language, with the model producing faithful interpretations of text prompts. However, expressing complex or nuanced ideas in text alone can be difficult.

arxiv-2402-11209.title: When Simple is Near Optimal in Security Games
arxiv-2402-11209.creator: Devansh Jalota, Michael Ostrovsky, Marco Pavone
arxiv-2402-11209.description: Abstract Fraud is ubiquitous across many applications and involves users bypassing the rule of law, often with the strategic aim of obtaining some benefit that would otherwise be unattainable within the bounds of lawful conduct. However, user fraud is detrimental, as it may compromise safety or impose disproportionate negative externalities on particular population groups.

arxiv-2408-03536.title: Anomalous Lasing Behavior in a Nonlinear Plasmonic Random Laser
arxiv-2408-03536.creator: Renu Yadav 1 , Sourabh Pal 2 , Subhajit Jana 1 , Samit K. Ray 1 Maruthi M. Brundavanam 1 , and Shivakiran Bhaktha B. N. 1
arxiv-2408-03536.description: Abstract An unprecedented double-threshold lasing behavior has been observed in a plasmonic random laser composed of Au nanoislands decorated on vertically standing ZnO nanorods, infiltrated with dye-doped polymer matrix. The strong coupling of random laser modes to plasmonic nanocavities results in a dominant absorption of the random laser emission, leading to the first unusual lasing threshold.

arxiv-2505-14345.title: Enhancing Classification with Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Using Distance-Based Sample Weights Thanks: This paper has been accepted for publication and oral presentation at the 2025 10th IEEE International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies (ICMLT 2025). The final authenticated version wil
arxiv-2505-14345.creator: Aydin Abedinia Dept. of Computer Science Islamic Azad University South-Tehran Branch Tehran, Iran abedinia.aydin@icloud.com Shima Tabakhi School of Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering Southern Illinois University Carbondale, United States Shima.tabakhi@siu.edu Vahid Seydi School of Ocean
arxiv-2505-14345.description: Abstract Recent advancements in semi-supervised deep learning have introduced effective strategies for leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data to improve classification performance. This work proposes a semi-supervised framework that utilizes a distance-based weighting mechanism to prioritize critical training samples based on their proximity to test data.

arxiv-2507-18725.title: The Right to be Forgotten in Pruning: Unveil Machine Unlearning on Sparse Models
arxiv-2507-18725.creator: Yang Xiao, Gen Li, Jie Ji, Ruimeng Ye, Xiaolong ma, Bo Hui
arxiv-2507-18725.description: Abstract Machine unlearning aims to efficiently eliminate the memory about deleted data from trained models and address the right to be forgotten. Despite the success of existing unlearning algorithms, unlearning in sparse models has not yet been well studied. In this paper, we empirically find that the deleted data has an impact on the pruned topology in a sparse model.

arxiv-2508-03043.title: Aerobatic maneuvers in insect-scale flapping-wing aerial robots via deep-learned robust tube model predictive control
arxiv-2508-03043.creator: Yi-Hsuan Hsiao, Andrea Tagliabue, Owen Matteson, Suhan Kim, [4pt] Tong Zhao, Jonathan P. How, YuFeng Chen, [10pt] Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139, USA
arxiv-2508-03043.description: Abstract Aerial insects exhibit highly agile maneuvers such as sharp braking, saccades, and body flips under disturbance. In contrast, insect-scale aerial robots are limited to tracking non-aggressive trajectories with small body acceleration. This performance gap is contributed by a combination of low robot inertia, fast dynamics, uncertainty in flapping-wing aerodynamics, and high susceptibility to environmental disturbance.

arxiv-2509-12509.title: Leveraging Machine Learning Force Fields (MLFFs) to Simulate Large Atomistic Systems for Fidelity Improvement of Superconducting Qubits and Sensors
arxiv-2509-12509.creator: Søren Smidstrup, Shela Aboud, Ricardo Borges, Anders Blom, Pankaj Aggarwal, Robert Freeman, and Jamil Kawa Synopsys, Inc Sunnyvale, CA 94085 Email: soren, sjaboud, ricardo, andersb, pankaja, ref, jamil@synopsys.com
arxiv-2509-12509.description: Abstract Materials engineering using atomistic modeling is an essential tool for the development of qubits and quantum sensors. Traditional density-functional theory (DFT) does however not adequately capture the complete physics involved, including key aspects and dynamics of superconductivity, surface states, etc.

arxiv-2602-14709.title: Deep Image Prior for Computed Tomography Reconstruction
arxiv-2602-14709.creator: Simon Arridge, Riccardo Barbano, Alexander Denker, Željko Kereta
arxiv-2602-14709.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Simon Arridge, Riccardo Barbano, Alexander Denker, Željko Kereta. We present a comprehensive overview of the Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework and its applications to image reconstruction in computed tomography. Unlike conventional deep learning methods that rely on large, supervised datasets, the DIP exploits the implicit bias of convolutional neural networks and operates in a fully unsupervised setting, requiring only a single measurement, even in the presence of noise.

britannica-1911-antibes.title: Antibes (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-antibes.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-antibes.description: Article 'Antibes' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. country produces an abundance of flowers. Antibes is the ancient Antipolis. It is said to have been founded before the Christian era (perhaps about 340 B.C.) by colonists from Marseilles, and is mentioned by Strabo. It was the seat of a bishopric from the 5th century to 1244, when the see was transferred to Grasse. William Augustus Brevoort Coolidge W.

cia-0000134270.title: General: Increased Soviet Press Attention to Cuba
cia-0000134270.creator: Central Intelligence Agency
cia-0000134270.source: Internet Archive — CIA Reading Room mirror
cia-0000134270.description: Declassified CIA document 0000134270, dated 1 November 1959. Subject: GENERAL: INCREASED SOVIET PRESS ATTENTION TO CUBA.

pmc-11382438.title: Resilience and Self-Compassion: Shields Against Age-Related Declines in Oral Health and Shame
pmc-11382438.creator: Christos Tsironis, Fotios Tatsis, Zoe Konstanti, Manolis Mentis, Konstantinos Stolakis, Vasiliki Kotsia, Stefanos Mantzoukas, Elena Dragioti, Mary Gouva
pmc-11382438.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the complex relationships between demographic factors, oral health indicators, self-compassion, and psychological well-being among elderly individuals by using a path model analysis.MethodsThe findings of this cross-sectional study are derived from data collected from a sample of 204 patients, including 120 females and 84 males, aged between 60 and 92 years, with an average age of 74.2 years (SD = 7.1).

pmc-11410296.title: An Unusual Presentation of an Amniotic Fluid Embolism: Fetal Bradycardia As the First Sign
pmc-11410296.creator: Vicki Wang, Taizoon Q Dhoon, John Steller, Dominic Carusillo, Ramin Rahimian, Shermeen Vakharia, Joseph Rinehart
pmc-11410296.description: Amniotic fluid embolism (AFE) is a potentially fatal maternal condition demanding awareness from obstetricians and anesthesiologists regarding its different manifestations. The typical presentation involves maternal respiratory distress, cardiovascular collapse, neurological changes, and coagulopathy followed by fetal distress.This unusual case study emphasizes that fetal compromise may precede maternal decompensation as the initial sign of AFE.

pmc-11516222.title: Strengthening Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in medical education via an intersectional approach
pmc-11516222.creator: G Hunting, O Hankivsky
pmc-11516222.description: BackgroundIn the wake of COVID-19, equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) policies have been taken up in the health field, yet the actual impact of these initiatives, particularly for multiply marginalized individuals, is debated. Despite progress in areas such as diversity promotion, EDI has been critiqued as superficial and as failing to challenge the drivers of health inequity.

pmc-11517074.title: User technology for AI-supported objective measurement of Work-related Quality of Life (MI-LQ)
pmc-11517074.creator: C Schreiber, M Geisler, J Voigt, H Kosakyan, J Hohn, A Hamm, E Mut, J M Burkhardt, U D Braumann, C Militzer-Horstmann
pmc-11517074.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundUnderstanding and enhancing job satisfaction is crucial for improving Work-Related Quality of Life (WrQoL) in today’s office work environments. Our work uses multimodal data collection and analysis techniques to objectively assess WrQoL, thus mitigating respondent bias and survey fatigue. Leveraging machine learning (ML) and automated methods measuring WrQoL presents a promising approach in public health research, particularly concerning stress-related health outcomes.MethodsThrough a systematic literature search of 9,242 publications to identify WrQoL indicators, we selected over 100 publications for data extraction.

pmc-11628727.title: Nuclear receptor Rev‐erbα alleviates intervertebral disc degeneration by recruiting NCoR–HDAC3 co‐repressor and inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome
pmc-11628727.creator: Qingshuang Zhou, Xiaojiang Pu, Zhuang Qian, Haojie Chen, Nannan Wang, Sinian Wang, Zhenhua Feng, Zezhang Zhu, Bin Wang, Yong Qiu, Xu Sun
pmc-11628727.description: Intervertebral discs (IVDs) are rhythmic tissues that experience daily low‐load recovery. Notably, aging and abnormal mechanical stress predispose IVDs to degeneration due to dysrhythmia‐induced disordered metabolism. Meanwhile, Rev‐erbα acts as a transcriptional repressor in maintaining biorhythms and homeostasis; however, its function in IVD homeostasis and degeneration remains unclear.

pmc-11644484.title: Insights into the Heat Shock Protein 70 (Hsp70) Family in Camelina sativa and Its Roles in Response to Salt Stress
pmc-11644484.creator: Parviz Heidari, Sadra Rezaee, Hadiseh Sadat Hosseini Pouya, Freddy Mora-Poblete
pmc-11644484.description: Hsp70s, a group of heat shock proteins, are ancient proteins that play a crucial part in maintaining the stability of cells when faced with various internal and external stresses. In this research, there are 72 CsHSP70 genes present and verified in Camelina sativa, all of which exhibit a wide range of physicochemical characteristics.

pmc-12502404.title: Responding to crisis: the intersection of police officer attitudes, organizational climate, and mental health crises
pmc-12502404.creator: Therese L Todd, Preeti Chauhan, Leah G Pope, Amy Watson
pmc-12502404.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPolice responses to people with serious mental illness (SMI) disproportionately result in negative outcomes, underscoring the importance of understanding the factors that may influence how police respond to mental health crises. Little research has examined officer attitudes toward mental illness, and no study has examined implicit bias toward mental illness among police officers or how bias and police departmental climate may impact outcomes in mental health crises.

pmc-12594528.title: The Effects of Theta-Gamma Peak Stimulation on Sensorimotor Learning During Speech Production
pmc-12594528.creator: Birtan Demirel, Daniel Lametti, Noa Alony Gilboa, Charlotte J Stagg, Kate E Watkins
pmc-12594528.description: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is a noninvasive neuromodulatory tool that is thought to entrain intrinsic neural oscillations by supplying low electric currents over the scalp. Recent work has demonstrated the efficacy of theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupled tACS over primary motor cortex to enhance motor skill acquisition and motor recovery after stroke.

pmc-12616471.title: Platelets facilitate fat grafting by mitochondrial transfer and reducing oxidative stress in adipose-derived stem cells
pmc-12616471.creator: Chen Ke, Kaibo Liu, Wanying Chen, Zhongming Cai, Fangfang Yang, Qing Wei, Yucang He, Jingping Wang, Liqun Li, Binting Ni
pmc-12616471.description: Autologous fat grafting (AFG), characterized by a broad tissue source and absence of immune rejection, is extensively utilized in plastic surgery. Despite its advantages, AFG is frequently challenged by a high rate of fat resorption and limited volume retention. Recent studies have increasingly focused on integrating platelet-related preparations with adipose tissue to enhance graft survival rates.

pmc-12650389.title: Population Dynamics and Body Size Structure of the Antarctic Krill Euphausia superba in the Bransfield Strait and South Shetland Islands
pmc-12650389.creator: Guoqing Zhao, Shuai Li, Jialiang Yang, Gangchen Zhang, Bo Xu, Hewei Liu, Xin Rao, Peng Lian, Hongliang Huang, Lingzhi Li
pmc-12650389.description: Simple SummaryAntarctic krill (Euphausia superba) is a key species in the marine ecosystem of the Antarctic Ocean, with important ecological and economic value. This study used 6 years of midwater trawl data (including over 160,000 krill length measurements) to study the spatio-temporal changes and population composition of Antarctic krill, aiming to provide useful advice for better fishery management.

pmc-12736005.title: Health Literacy in Pregnant Women and Its Associations with Personal, Socioeconomic, and Health-Related Factors in Primary Care
pmc-12736005.creator: Evaristo Iván Vicente-Díaz, Myriam Alvariñas-Villaverde, Antonio Martinez-Sabater, Elena Chover-Sierra, Carles Saus-Ortega
pmc-12736005.description: Background/Objectives: Health literacy (HL) plays a fundamental role in maternal and neonatal outcomes by influencing women’s ability to access, understand, and apply health information during pregnancy. However, evidence regarding the determinants of HL among pregnant women remains limited, particularly within the Spanish context.

pmc-12971943.title: Quality and reliability of semaglutide content on different Chinese short video platforms: a study focusing on side effects
pmc-12971943.creator: Jiayuan Song, Xingchen He, Zhenhai Cui, Ye Sun, Yanlin Liu, Han Yu, Aimin Li, Meiying Jin
pmc-12971943.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the quality, reliability, and content characteristics of semaglutide-related short videos on three major Chinese short-video platforms (Bilibili, TikTok, and Rednote), with a focus on exploring differences in the presentation of side effects across different platforms and uploader types.

pmc-13056267.title: Reliability of the E-test and VITEK 2 Compact for Tigecycline Susceptibility Testing in Clinical Acinetobacter baumannii Isolates Compared With Broth Microdilution
pmc-13056267.creator: Amresh Pati, Bilal Ahmad Malik, Kavita Gupta, Ashoka Mahapatra
pmc-13056267.description: Background: The growing incidence of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (MDR AB) has left very limited therapeutic options. Tigecycline, the first antibiotic in the glycylcycline class, is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) for the treatment of complicated intra-abdominal infections and complicated skin and skin structure infections.

pmc-13156404.title: Phytochemical Composition, Health Benefits, Functional Properties, and Food Applications of Pumpkin Seeds
pmc-13156404.creator: Messenbet Geremew Kassa, Desye Alemu Teferi
pmc-13156404.description: Pumpkin seeds ( Cucurbita pepo ) are increasingly recognized as a functional food due to their rich composition of proteins, healthy lipids, dietary fiber, and essential micronutrients. They have traditionally been consumed for culinary and therapeutic purposes. This review highlights the chemical composition, bioactive compounds, health‐promoting potential, and applications of pumpkin seeds in food systems.

pmc-13211000.title: Holistic Performance Programming for mTBI Recovery in U.S. Military Tactical Athletes: A Narrative Review
pmc-13211000.creator: Ed Daly, John Mackersie, Lisa Ryan
pmc-13211000.description: Tactical athletes, including military service members, are exposed to occupational demands that increase their risk of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), particularly through blast exposure, falls, collisions, and repeated sub-concussive events. Although clinical tools and progressive return-to-activity protocols support acute management, recovery may remain fragmented when physical, cognitive, psychological, and performance domains are not integrated.

pmc-13297297.title: Nonlinear EEG Complexity as a Marker of Maladaptive Brain Plasticity in Substance Use Disorders: A Multi-Group Machine Learning Classification Study
pmc-13297297.creator: Mashal Fatima, Faraz Akram, Imran Khan Niazi
pmc-13297297.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Across six substance use groups and control participants without a diagnosis of substance use disorder (n = 350; 50 per group), all four nonlinear EEG complexity measures (LLE, FD, HE, KC) were significantly reduced in users, with the largest losses in frontal and central regions linked to motor planning and sensorimotor integration.

pmc-13473002.title: A hydrogel platform delivering mesenchymal stem cell lysate for potential myocardial tissue repair
pmc-13473002.creator: Ziwei Du, Qi Zhang, Qiuhua Wang, Paul Santerre, Tianyi Ma, Peng Ma, Xiaoqing Zhang
pmc-13473002.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionMyocardial infarction is one of the most significant causes of death worldwide and the limited regenerative capacity of the myocardium often results in poor recovery after injury. Stem cell therapy has some promise for myocardial tissue repair, but clinical translation is hindered by poor cell survival and safety concerns, prompting the investigations of cell-free strategies such as stem cell-derived secretome or lysate.MethodsIn this study, a quaternized chitosan/tannic acid hydrogel was fabricated and characterized for its crosslinking stability, injectability and degradation kinetics.

pmc-13506261.title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation liberation before heart transplantation in the modern allocation era: Predictors and one-year outcomes from the National OPTN/UNOS Registry
pmc-13506261.creator: Admire Hlupeni, Kevin Montes, Mehran Jalilzadehbinazar, Adebisi Adejola, Rayvlin J Liceralde, Hussain AM Khan, Adekunle Obisesan
pmc-13506261.description: BackgroundThe clinical significance of ECMO liberation before heart transplantation remains poorly defined.ObjectivesTo identify predictors of pre-transplant ECMO liberation and evaluate its association with 1-year post-transplant survival.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the national OPTN/UNOS registry, including adult isolated heart transplant recipients supported with ECMO at listing between October 18, 2018 and March 31, 2026.

pmc-13578105.title: 7 Tesla MRI with Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping: qualitative grading and quantitative focal measurements of the substantia nigra as a potential biomarker for Parkinson’s disease
pmc-13578105.creator: Runa G Unsgård, Kjersti E Stige, Anne L Kristoffersen, Pål E Goa, Charalampos Tzoulis, Erik M Berntsen
pmc-13578105.description: PurposeParkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss in the substantia nigra (SN). Imaging biomarkers sensitive to nigral pathology are limited. This study evaluated susceptibility changes in the SN using quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) at 7 Tesla MRI, and explored associations with clinical variables.

pmc-13632133.title: Cardiovascular health and depression among postpartum women in the United States
pmc-13632133.creator: Megan M McLaughlin, Catherine Lee, Xiaoning Huang, Nisha I Parikh, Kristina M Deligiannidis, Sadiya S Khan, Alexis L Beatty
pmc-13632133.description: BackgroundThe postpartum period is a critical time period for both cardiovascular health (CVH) and psychosocial health among women. While depression is a recognized cardiovascular risk factor in non-pregnant populations, the association between depression and CVH in the postpartum period has been understudied.ObjectivesTo examine the association between depression and CVH among reproductive-age women and whether postpartum status modifies this association.

wallace-contributions-natural-selection-.title: Contributions to the Theory of Natural Selection
wallace-contributions-natural-selection-.creator: Alfred Russel Wallace
wallace-contributions-natural-selection-.description: Wallace's 1870 collection of essays including 'The Limits of Natural Selection as applied to Man' — the co-discoverer of natural selection arguing, controversially, that human intellect required more than selection alone. A founding document of evolutionary anthropology.
